alex_w: Heads up — noticed a spike in tail latency on Mixtral-7B for long-context workloads after yesterday's kernel prefetch change + batching heuristic rollout. p99 ~2.1x higher, p50 roughly same. Linking prod trace in thread.
maria_s: Saw it on canary as well. Quick repro locally with long prompts: latencies start OK then jump around token ~4k-5k. Reproducer and profiler attached to the canary run.
chen_k: Profiler snippet from the failing run (trimmed):
```
step=4590 seq_pos=8123 batch=1 gpu_ms=120 cpu_ms=5 kv_cache_hits=0 prefetch_async=true kernel=tiling_v2 mem_used_mb=18312 kv_evictions=3
step=4591 seq_pos=8124 batch=1 gpu_ms=420 cpu_ms=6 kv_cache_hits=0 prefetch_async=true kernel=tiling_v2 mem_used_mb=18640 kv_evictions=8
```
Notice the big jump in gpu_ms when kv_evictions spike.
samir_p: Interesting — Qwen workloads didn't show this. I think mixing tiled kernel prefetch with the new batching heuristic increases concurrent KV working set at the tail. The heuristic now batches more aggressively across pending requests which inflates peak memory pressure.
katie_d: We also saw quality regressions in long-context QA evals for Mixtral after the kernel swap — approx 3% absolute drop on the long-qa shard. Diff looks correlated with a RoPE fallback flip in the runtime when prefetch triggers evictions.
perf-bot: perf/regression-alert: task=tail-latency severity=high p99_ratio=2.1 triggered_by=canary
alex_w: Repro script (local):
```
# reproduce locally
python scripts/bench.py --model mixtral-7b --tokens 16000 --batch 1 --prefetch on --batching adaptive_v2 --prompts tests/long_prompts.jsonl
```
maria_s: Bisection points to commit abc1234 which introduced `prefetch:tile-async` + `adaptive_v2` batching tweaks. Reverting prefetch on canary brings p99 back down to baseline in our runs.
chen_k: Hypothesis: async prefetch issues with tiled memory layout -> extra allocations/evictions for KV pages. Mixtral's config (heads=64, kv_dim=128) seems to make it especially sensitive due to denser KV per token. Two mitigations:
- disable prefetch for seq_len > 4096
- or add a memory-threshold guard: if kv_mem_fraction > 0.75 then skip prefetch
samir_p: Practical hotfix: add kernel-selector rule: if model in mixtral_family AND seq_len>4096 then force kernel=tiling_v1 and prefetch=false. Roll this to 10% canary and observe.
katie_d: Also run long-context eval suite before expanding the rollout. We need to confirm quality regression is eliminated by the heuristic (not just latency improvements).
deploy-bot: rollout request submitted: /kernel-selector patch v2 -> canary 10% by samir_p at 1968000024
alex_w: I'll open PR with the heuristic + unit tests + reproducer and attach perf numbers (before/after). I'll also schedule deeper NVTX/nvprof memory tracing for Mixtral long sequences.
maria_s: Thanks. Keep this thread updated. If canary shows any downstream regressions we will rollback prefetch change entirely. :thumbsup:
